vehicles.headline: Used petrol AWD with a practical second row
vehicles.summary: A lower-cost petrol alternative with all-wheel drive and a full-size spare. Related BabyDrive evidence supports a three-seat trial; check the actual seats, service history and remaining warranty.

range.basis: Not applicable: petrol-only; no electric driving range.

consumption.basis: Australian ADR 81/02 combined laboratory fuel consumption; not a real-world guarantee.

depletedConsumption.basis: Not applicable: petrol-only vehicle, not a plug-in hybrid.

length.basis: MY22–MY24 facelift: 4,640 mm. MY21 pre-facelift is 4,625 mm; confirm build/model year.

vehicles.warranty: 5 years / unlimited km for private use from original delivery; confirm remaining cover.
vehicles.servicing: Every 12 months / 12,500 km, whichever first. Used-car budget includes post-cap uncertainty.

safety.applicability: Australian S5 Forester, September 2018–May 2025, all variants including hybrids. Historical 2019 test protocol; not the new S6 rating.

familyFit.summary: Three restraints fitted in BabyDrive’s earlier S5 Premium, using all three vehicle seatbelts. This 2.5i-L is a related grade/year; your own seats remain pending.
familyFit.row2: Two outer ISOFIX positions; three rear top-tether anchors. Centre installation uses the vehicle belt.
familyFit.testedSeats: Related 2019 S5 Premium: rear-facing Britax Unity capsule + rear-facing Britax Graphene outside, forward-facing Britax Maxi Guard Pro centre. All three used vehicle belts to gain width.
familyFit.buckleAccess: Three-booster buckle access was not established. Test every buckle and the roof-mounted centre belt in this car.
familyFit.access: Large rear door openings in the related test; load your children and restraints during inspection.
familyFit.ventilation: Rear console air vents; confirm airflow with all three restraints installed.

pros: Used asking prices below the A$45,000 target.
AWD, full-size spare and a 1,800 kg braked towing limit.
cons: 12,500 km servicing means more than one visit a year at 15,000 km.
Petrol fuel use is higher than the hybrids in the shortlist.
Earlier test used a mixed-facing combination; your three forward-facing seats or boosters need checking.
inspection: Read the build plate: late-2021 MY22 facelift cars differ from MY21.
Ask for dated 12,500 km service invoices, coolant history and any thermo-control-valve diagnosis/replacement.
Road test the CVT cold and warm; ask a Subaru specialist to diagnose warnings, shudder or leaks.
Load-test the 12 V battery and test air-conditioning, EyeSight, cameras and every restraint buckle.

changes.text: MY22 facelift arrived in late 2021; body length increases from 4,625 to 4,640 mm, with revised styling and driver assistance. This group keeps the 2.5i-L petrol powertrain; inspect year-specific equipment.
Subaru’s MY23 notice lists only higher-grade mirror/colour changes; do not assume those are additions to 2.5i-L.

gaps: No exact MY21–MY24 2.5i-L three-booster trial verified.
Price sample is small and spans different kilometres and fee bases.
Australian model-specific repair incidence and installed major-repair quotes are unavailable.

vehicles.generation: S6 / SL · Australian MY26 new generation
vehicles.headline: The new Forester, with the petrol drivetrain
vehicles.summary: New-generation MY26 petrol AWD, sold locally from June 2025. Its related Hybrid Sport family test fitted three forward-facing seats. Petrol retains a full-size spare and has a higher towing limit than the hybrid.

familyFit.summary: BabyDrive fitted three forward-facing seats in the new-generation Hybrid Sport. Useful same-generation evidence for this petrol AWD, with the tested grade/powertrain difference kept visible.

familyFit.testedSeats: Related July 2025 S6 Hybrid Sport: three forward-facing seats, or two forward-facing plus one rear-facing behind the driver. Article does not identify every restraint model.
familyFit.buckleAccess: No matching petrol-base three-booster buckle test verified. Check belt receivers and independent installation of each restraint.
familyFit.access: Related test found room for a 186 cm driver ahead of a rear-facing seat; verify your driving position.
familyFit.ventilation: Rear console air vents, documented in the new-generation family test and Australian specification.

pros: 15,000 km service interval and published capped prices.
Petrol version retains a spare wheel and 1,800 kg braked towing.
cons: 7.9 L/100 km laboratory combined figure; city use can be substantially higher.
New examples sit near the A$45,000 limit; obtain a Queensland drive-away quote.
Long-term S6 fault data is limited; the published three-seat trial was a Hybrid Sport.
inspection: Confirm S6/MY26; 2025 sale/build year can also describe the outgoing S5.
Trial three restraints and the pram in this petrol base, including booster buckle access.
Test driver-monitor alerts and wireless phone connection during an ordinary family drive.
Confirm first-delivery warranty date and any dealer extension conditions in writing.

changes.text: New S6 generation: 2.5 petrol is 136 kW / 247 Nm, 7.9 L/100 km ADR combined, 496 L rear-seat-up boot, 15,000 km service interval. Separate from the 6.2 L/100 km strong hybrid.

gaps: One exact QLD new-stock seller advertisement found atA$44,990; fresh QLD fetch blocked. A confirmed current Queensland delivered quote is still needed.
No direct petrol-base three-restraint test or long-term S6 repair-cost average verified.

vehicles.generation: BT / sixth generation · Australian 2.5 naturally aspirated
vehicles.headline: A roomy used wagon with AWD
vehicles.summary: The standard non-turbo 2.5-litre Outback gives a long boot and 2,000 kg braked towing. BabyDrive’s same-generation Sport fitted a mixed-facing three-restraint combination; this base grade keeps a separate fit check.

safety.applicability: BT Outback all variants built from December 2020, Australian sale from March 2021; expiry December 2027. Does not describe the new seventh-generation 2026 Outback.

familyFit.summary: BabyDrive’s 2021 Outback Sport fitted two forward-facing and one rear-facing restraint. Related same-generation evidence for the base AWD; your exact combination remains pending.
familyFit.row2: Two outer ISOFIX pairs and three top tethers on rear seatbacks; the centre vehicle belt comes from the roof.
familyFit.testedSeats: 2021 Sport test reports two forward-facing and one rear-facing child seat. Restraint model names are not supplied in the reviewed article.
familyFit.buckleAccess: The roof-mounted centre belt was awkward in the test. Three-booster buckle access is not established.
familyFit.access: Rear doors and rear legroom suited the tested combination; trial your own seats and final front-seat positions.
familyFit.ventilation: Rear console vents and two rear USB ports in the tested generation; check the actual car.

pros: Long 522 L luggage area with all five seats occupied.
Full-size spare, AWD and 2,000 kg braked towing.
Used base examples can cost substantially less than A$45,000.
cons: 4.87 m length requires a parking-space check.
Non-turbo engine is less forceful when loaded.
12,500 km service interval and touchscreen climate controls need consideration.
inspection: Confirm standard 2.5 base AWD: exclude XT/turbo, Sport/Touring and 2026 seventh-generation advertisements.
Check both MY21 EyeSight braking recalls by VIN and ask for completion evidence.
Verify service invoices, coolant/TCV history, CVT operation and 12 V battery health.
Try the roof-mounted centre belt with all restraints installed and inspect windscreen/EyeSight operation.
Check REC-005830/SRT351 inhibitor-switch rectification by VIN, including camera and reverse lamps; applicable remedy is free.

changes.text: New BT generation with 138 kW / 245 Nm naturally aspirated 2.5, 7.3 L/100 km ADR combined and 522 L rear-seat-up boot.
Infotainment and safety equipment changed during the generation; verify the exact build. XT turbo variants are excluded from this base 2.5 configuration.

gaps: Current price cohort consists of 2021 MY21 examples, not every 2021–2025 year.
No exact base-grade three-forward-facing or three-booster test verified.
Australian installed CVT/TCV repair quotes and representative failure rates remain unavailable.

ownership.serviceInterval: S5/MY21–MY24: 12 months or 12,500 km. S6/MY26: 12 months or 15,000 km. Whichever first.
ownership.serviceBasis: ESTIMATE: MY24 petrol Forester first five capped visits total A$2,674.64 over 62,500 km. At 15,000 km/year a distance-scaled reference is about A$642/year, then allow post-cap / older-used uncertainty: A$750/year planning budget (A$600–1,100). At this mileage a sixth service can be due within five years; confirm all remaining due visits. Scheduled maintenance is separate from repairs and tyres.
warrantyCautions: Private-use manufacturer cover is five years / unlimited kilometres from original supply, not from your used-car purchase. Commercial/hire/ride-share uses have a 150,000 km limit; check the contract.
Dealer-backed extended warranties can have conditions and are separate from Subaru’s manufacturer warranty. Do not assume a photographed or advertised ten-year dealer scheme applies.
Australian Consumer Law rights are separate from the written warranty; ask for the VIN-specific warranty and recall status.
The October 2026 REC-006737 parking-pawl campaign is for 42 selected Forester Hybrid VINs. It is not assigned to this petrol S6 configuration.

risks.title: CVT / AWD drivetrain inspection
risks.detail: A major gearbox or engine repair can exceed a small annual reserve. Inspect cold and hot operation, leaks, warnings and service invoices. No representative Australian failure rate for these exact configurations was found.
risks.priceBasis: Unpriced: no exact Australian installed quote verified. Obtain a VIN-specific diagnosis and written parts/labour/GST quote; do not transfer prices or failure rates from older Subarus.
risks.warranty: Manufacturing-defect cover depends on the original warranty, diagnosis, service history and exclusions; wear and external damage differ.

risks.title: Thermo-control valve — inspect early used cars
risks.detail: Subaru’s US bulletin identifies coolant-vapour intrusion into an electronic valve sensor on selected 2019–2021 Forester and 2020–2022 Outback vehicles and describes a revised part. This is an inspection lead for an early used example, not proof that every Australian car is affected or that later years use the same part.
risks.priceBasis: Unpriced: an Australian installed repair quote and incidence were not verified. Ask for diagnostic codes and any replacement invoice.
risks.warranty: The US 15-year / 150,000-mile extension is not an Australian warranty entitlement. Ask Subaru Australia to confirm VIN-specific support before paying.

forester-awd-petrol-2025.serviceBasis: Australian MY26 S6 petrol capped visits: A$347.95,520.45,393.10,679.30 and 358.20 = A$2,299 for first five services / five years / 75,000 km; A$459.80/year at 15,000 km/year.
